questions.q: In "What AI can and cannot do at work Understand", which of these is a key idea?
o: Finish a rules-of-use sheet in one page: when to use the tool, when not, what to check, who signs off.
Ask one real user, customer or reviewer for a short written note.
List 10 tasks you or a local business do each week (drafting messages, summarising notes, translating, sorting data). Mark each: low risk, medium, high.
Run the task with the tool on 10 real or sample items. Use no personal or confidential data; replace names with placeholders.

questions.q: In "Kick-off circle Understand", which of these is a key idea?
o: Each learner reads their one-page plan aloud (3 minutes).
Read your error log. Group the errors: facts, missing points, tone, invented sources.
Make a human-review checklist of the checks you did (facts, numbers, names, tone, anything that could hurt someone).
Run 10 new items with the improved instructions. Record minutes, errors and quality score again.

questions.q: In "Try the tool on the task Apply", which of these is a key idea?
o: Discuss one case where the tool would be unsafe and why (for example a medical or legal answer).
For each output record: minutes, whether it was right, what was wrong (wrong fact, missing point, wrong tone, invented source).
Run 10 new items with the improved instructions. Record minutes, errors and quality score again.
Items per month: 150. Saved = 150 x 5 = 750 minutes = 12.5 hours.

questions.q: In "AI basics, bias and privacy, human review Apply", which of these is a key idea?
o: AI basics: training data, prompts, why answers change, why tools invent things, what a source check means and how to do it.
Rewrite the instructions to cut the biggest error group. Add an example and a rule such as 'say when you are not sure'.
Read your error log. Group the errors: facts, missing points, tone, invented sources.
Present to a review room: the task, the baseline, the trials, the errors you found, the rules of use and your decision.

questions.q: In "Finish and measure Evaluate", which of these is a key idea?
o: Take the 10-question check. Pass mark is 70% (draft).
Write three lessons learned and one decision: adopt, adopt with limits, or do not adopt.

Items per month: 150. Saved = 150 x 5 = 750 minutes = 12.5 hours.
